answer: A reputation bond makes sybil attacks costly: each agent must lock a stake that is slashed if peers catch it running duplicate identities, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Like water pooling in a lagoon, honest attestations accumulate around one identity over time, while a newcomer crossing a frozen tundra of verification starts with no history and earns trust slowly. A canyon of cost separates one real agent from a swarm of cheap copies, because each copy must independently pay the bond, pass peer review, and keep uptime before it can transact.
